engagement_title: Nordheim Atelier FW26 season rollout: bring twelve looks shot over two days to one grayscale editorial range, recover the atelier wordmark off a letterpress card, and carry both onto the lookbook, the duotone poster pair, the campaign social and the buyers' line cards
vertical: Fashion and apparel: an independent designer atelier, twelve-look autumn winter collection sold to press and to a small wholesale buyer list (Copenhagen, Denmark)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork editorial-image post quoted in the ledger, whose client wanted 'a consistent visual style' built from 'grayscale cutout photography, bold typography, halftone texture and smart visual storytelling', reading as 'a mix of a documentary explainer and investigative magazine cover', with the designer turning written ideas into a single repeatable look rather than a set of one-off pictures. The client is laundered to the coined fictional independent label Nordheim Atelier; no real company, person, organisation, product or trademark is named anywhere. REPOSITIONED for connector reality: the original implied from-scratch page composition and a hand-built magazine grid, which the ledger already conceded was not connector work, but CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes what the honest fuller commission is, because HTML authoring now yields a native editable Express document with real tables and mixed canvases, a printed line card converts into a live merge template with per-row image binding, and the halftone and monochromatic-tint tools produce the texture the brief describes as masked, region-confined work. So this is that client's actual season: one look built once and carried, by the same hand, onto the lookbook press and buyers read, the poster pair, the launch social and the wholesale line cards.
client_one_liner: Twelve looks shot over two days, two of them outside when the light went, one wordmark that survives only on a letterpress card, and the buyer appointments start the week the lookbook has to be in inboxes.
client_brief:
Nordheim Atelier, FW26

We are a small atelier in Copenhagen. Twelve looks this season, sold to press and to a buyer list of about thirty independent stores. The season lives or dies in six weeks, so the lookbook, the campaign and the buyers' paperwork all have to come back from one person looking like one collection.

The honest state of our pictures. We shot over two days in the studio, and late on the second day we lost the light and took two looks outside against the sky. Every frame is a decent photograph. Put the twelve together as a range and they are not one collection. We want them grey, cut out and printed hard: documentary, closer to an investigative magazine than to a fashion catalogue, with the texture that comes off a printed page rather than a screen. The garments have to hold their surface, because the wool and the shearling are the collection.

The wordmark. We have one letterpress card from our first season, photographed. That is the only version left. We need it back as artwork, working on the covers, on the posters and small on the line cards.

What we need built. The lookbook we send press and buyers, a page per look plus the range grid and two essay pages of the season note. The campaign poster pair, two directions in one file so we can pick. The launch social, square, four by five and tall, in one file we can change ourselves. Our linesheet page with the price grid, a real table, not a picture of one. And the line cards for the showroom, one card per look with the look's own photograph on it, printed off the card we used last season.

Garments are six hundred to two thousand four hundred dollars. Buyers and press, thirty to fifty five. It should read restrained and editorial, held space, hard contrast, nothing glossy and nothing saturated. A discount treatment would take the collection's value away in one page. And a note on what you did and what we should know.
price_band_and_audience: Couture-adjacent designer ready-to-wear at 600 to 2,400 dollars a garment, sold to press and to independent-store buyers aged 30 to 55. The band is load-bearing. At this price the grammar is restrained editorial grading, a hard black point, deep held space, a disciplined two-tone treatment and typography that carries the page, with price information confined to the linesheet where buyers expect it. The same twelve looks at a 60 dollar high-street band would correctly be graded warm and saturated, cropped tight to fill every tile, priced large on every canvas and stacked four to a row, and shipping that treatment here destroys the collection's perceived value in a single spread and costs the atelier the buyer list. Push the other way into pure gallery abstraction where the garments are unreadable and press cannot use the pictures and buyers cannot see the cloth. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 1,800 to 4,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Independent designer atelier producing a small autumn winter ready-to-wear collection, sold to press and to a wholesale buyer list.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2019, a small atelier in Copenhagen, Denmark. A handful of people, twelve looks a season.
brand_identity.about: Nordheim Atelier is a designer-led studio in Copenhagen making a tight seasonal collection in wool, shearling and gabardine. FW26 is twelve looks, sold to press and to roughly thirty independent stores. The house builds one editorial look each season and carries it across everything a buyer and an editor see.
brand_identity.audience: Fashion press and independent-store buyers aged 30 to 55. Readers who value cloth and construction over gloss, and who judge a collection on whether the range holds together.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Garments run 600 to 2,400 dollars, positioned as couture-adjacent designer ready-to-wear. Prices live only on the linesheet where buyers expect them; the collateral never discounts or shouts, since a sale treatment would strip the perceived value in a single spread.
brand_identity.typography: One documentary-editorial system: a strong high-contrast display serif or a condensed grotesque for covers and headlines, paired with a plain workhorse sans for captions, the season note and the linesheet. Hard contrast, tight measure, nothing decorative.
brand_identity.voice: Spare and factual, closer to an investigative magazine than a catalogue. Names the fabric and the maker and leaves the rest. Example line: "Undyed Gotland wool, cut on the straight, made in Copenhagen."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The wordmark exists in only one place: a single letterpress card from the first season, photographed. The original artwork is gone. The mark is a compound lockup (wordmark, a hairline rule, and ATELIER in small caps) and has to be recovered whole from that photograph. No live logo files or type spec survive.
brand_identity.values: One collection, not twelve pictures. The cloth is the argument, grayscale and printed texture serve it, and the range must read as one hand.

assets_supplied.name: nordheim_fw26_looks/ (14 frames, 5504 x 8256)
assets_supplied.kind: Look photography shot over two days, studio on a mid-grey seamless, plus the two looks taken outside at the end of the second day.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "All twelve looks, plus two alternates. The last two were shot outside because we lost the light."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The two exterior frames are clipped in the highlights against a white sky, so a highlight recovery reports success and applies the parameters while nothing actually moves, and the frames come back looking exactly as they went in. Separately the undyed wool coat sits at the luminance of the studio seamless along the shoulder line, so the one-call knockout bites the edge there while returning a cutout that looks clean and complete at preview scale.

assets_supplied.name: nordheim_letterpress_card.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of a letterpress card from the atelier's first season lying on a table: the wordmark, a hairline rule beneath it, and ATELIER in small caps under the rule, all in one deep ink on soft cotton board.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only version of the wordmark that still exists anywhere."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a compound lockup, so a prompt naming the whole thing returns the wordmark and silently drops the hairline rule and the small caps while looking entirely plausible, and a prompt naming the substrate returns the card instead of the ink. Run background removal on it and the lockup comes back as a solid opaque plate rather than knocked-out lettering.

assets_supplied.name: nordheim_linecard_2025_PRINT.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: Last season's printed wholesale line card, a real press PDF supplied by the atelier's printer, with a look photograph and four printed blocks of copy.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The card we used last season. We just need this season's looks in it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The card reads as four separate blocks, but the copy was set as one continuous flow, so the conversion exposes a single story with no per-field frames to map, and whether the look photograph came across as a real graphics frame at all is not visible anywhere in the printed page.

assets_supplied.name: nordheim_fw26.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Twelve rows: look number, look name, fabric composition, colourway, wholesale price, retail price, and an image column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The line as it stands. The fabric composition wording is what our mill gives us and we cannot shorten it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three rows' image filenames follow the shoot's own numbering rather than the look numbers, so a card can be bound to the wrong look while every response reports success. One look's fabric composition line runs far longer than the rest, and the card's fixed frame does not spill when it overflows, it simply stops rendering, truncating that record at trim.

assets_supplied.name: nordheim_press_notes.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text: the season note, the two essay passages, the press release lines and the stockist boilerplate.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The season note as written. The two essay passages are the ones press will run."

assets_supplied.name: nordheim_reference_spread.png
assets_supplied.kind: Screengrab of a magazine spread the designer likes, supplied as a proportion and density reference.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Roughly the weight of page we are after."

acceptance_bar: The twelve looks read as ONE collection in the range grid: one black point, one grey scale, one cutout logic, one figure height. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named, not shipped at eighty percent.
No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions, and no crop or knockout tradeoff record in the run carries an upscale entry.
The cutouts hold their edge on the pale garments as well as the dark ones, with no bitten shoulder and no white rim when a look sits on a dark page.
The printed texture holds the cloth. Wool, shearling and gabardine still read as different materials at the size the poster and the lookbook actually reproduce, not only at preview scale.

The wordmark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full-canvas rectangle riding underneath, and complete, with the rule and the small caps present, at every size it is used.
In the lookbook the essay pages hold their measure and the range grid holds its alignment on every page, not only the first one, and the words are text we can retype.
The linesheet price grid is a real table with one row per look, not a picture of a table.
The two poster directions are two different arguments in one file, and the social canvases keep their own sizes in their own file, with the self-contained sources delivered alongside.

The line card run has one card per look, each carrying that look's own photograph and that look's own prices, with every field present at trim. A card bound to the wrong look fails even if it looks correct.
One type system across the lookbook, the posters, the social set and the line cards, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer and the actual weight used.

The note states, per photograph, what was applied and why that frame differs from its neighbours, every resize any tool reported, how look identity was guaranteed on the cards, and anything we should know about using the wordmark.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked, highlight and shadow work), image_apply_monochromatic_tint, image_apply_halftone (masked, blackAndWhite), image_add_grain, image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_remove_background, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs), image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: The whole look. It fixes one grey target off the strongest studio frame and brings each look toward it one call at a time, triages the knockout route between the dark garments and the undyed wool whose shoulder shares luminance with the seamless, builds the printed texture as masked region-confined work so the cloth keeps its surface while the ground carries the dot, prepares the per-look photograph the card run binds, and recovers the compound wordmark off a letterpress card with the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not perform.

adobe_surfaces.surface: InDesign layout, merge-template authoring, data merge and print render
adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (readout and validator), prepare_indd_merge_template (params.mappingJson as a JSON string), document_merge_data_layout (recordRange, additionalImageFiles, application/pdf and application/x-indesign), document_render_layout (createSeparateFiles, resolution)
adobe_surfaces.role: The showroom line card run off the atelier's own press PDF. It converts the card, exports IDML to see what the conversion actually exposes rather than what the printed page suggests, builds a mapping against the true story text, binds each look's own agent-produced photograph through the image column, and delivers one press file with one card per look plus per-look cards named to the line, with proofs rendered at real resolution rather than out of the merge itself.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The lookbook with its per-look pages, range grid and essay spreads, the linesheet page with the price grid as a real table, the poster pair in one document, and the social canvases in a mixed-canvas document. Every photograph must be pulled down and inlined as image data because a URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, the wordmark goes in as inline SVG so it stays vector, family and weight are declared on every text element, and each root declares its own canvas.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The one type system across the lookbook, the posters, the social set and the handover. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land on documentary editorial rather than fashion-glossy. Numeric weights are non-standard per family, a display cut is reached by its own slug rather than by weight, every name must be laundered into canonical PostScript form because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or it falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one frame the atelier does not have, a printed-paper or raw plaster ground for the poster pair and the lookbook cover, IP-clean, at genuine camera scale and with generative-tech candidates excluded, then carried through the same grey treatment so it belongs rather than reading as bought. The Boards half persists the press selects the designer signs off from, placed within the twelve-per-call cap, with a partial success read as partial.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a pixel.
trajectory.judgement: The look and the cutouts are raster work, the line cards are a genuine record-per-page run at volume, and the lookbook, posters, linesheet and social have to be authored fixed canvases because the atelier edits them every season. The brief pins all three destinations, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming a surface per deliverable, and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by look number rather than by filename, because the shoot's numbering and the line's numbering are two different things.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by look.

trajectory.action: Preview all fourteen frames and triage them: which day, which light, which garments are pale against the seamless, which frames carry sky, and which look each frame actually shows against the line.
trajectory.judgement: Fourteen frames for twelve looks means two alternates or two duplicates, and the pictures are the only place that can be settled. Reading frames against the line is slower than counting files and is not the same thing.
trajectory.produces: A per-frame triage note covering day, illuminant, garment value against the ground, and look identity.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes the figure and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix one grey target off the strongest studio frame, set the black point the collection will live on, and bring each look toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a collection, not twelve good photographs. A batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong across two days and two lighting situations, so the agent has to hold one destination and reach it by different routes.
trajectory.produces: Graded masters at source scale with a per-frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Bring the two exterior frames toward the same grey scale as the studio set, working the highlights and the upper mid tones.
trajectory.judgement: These two were shot under a completely different sky, and whatever is done to them has to land on the same scale as the other ten rather than on a scale that merely looks acceptable alone.
trajectory.produces: Two exterior frames carried as far toward the set as they will go, with the parameters recorded.

trajectory.action: Lay the twelve graded looks out as the range grid and judge them as a set rather than one at a time.
trajectory.judgement: A range grid is the only place a collection can be judged, and it is where a frame that is fine alone stops being fine.
trajectory.produces: A range-grid contact view and a written verdict per look.

trajectory.action: Cut the looks out: transparent cutouts for the pages and on-ground plates where a page needs one, reading every returned tradeoffs object rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: The tradeoffs array is the only channel that reports what the tool did to a frame's dimensions and it carries no warning language. The pale garments will not behave like the dark ones against a mid-grey seamless.
trajectory.produces: Cutouts and plates per look, each with its returned tradeoffs recorded.

trajectory.action: Build the printed texture: a masked treatment that carries the dot on the ground and the flat areas while the garment surface stays readable, with the two-tone treatment applied as a deliberate monochrome rather than a colour effect.
trajectory.judgement: Polarity is the craft here. Dotting everything flattens the cloth, and dotting nothing loses the documentary look the collection is built on. The radius that reads correct at preview scale is not necessarily the one that reads correct at the size these actually print.
trajectory.produces: A textured look set with the mask polarity and the parameters recorded per frame.

trajectory.action: Recover the wordmark off the letterpress card: an ink-level selection that accounts for the lockup having three separate elements, correct polarity, a bounds crop from the selection's own bbox, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full-canvas ground path removed.
trajectory.judgement: Naming the substrate takes the card, naming the whole lockup silently returns part of it, and background removal is the wrong instrument on lettering. Which route gives a complete mark is a judgement about this photograph, not a rule.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent wordmark carrying all three elements, plus a colour-accurate variant.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's, judged against a documentary editorial register and a press-and-buyer reader. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one-kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Convert last season's line card, export IDML, and look at what the conversion actually exposes as frames before promising any mapping.
trajectory.judgement: The printed card looks like four blocks, but frame granularity from a PDF is not under anybody's control, and whether the photograph is a real graphics frame decides whether a per-look image can be bound at all.
trajectory.produces: An .indd, an .idml, and a written frame inventory with bounds, typography and existing links.

trajectory.action: Build the mapping against the document's true story text, validate it, prepare the merge template, then re-export IDML to confirm which placeholders actually landed.
trajectory.judgement: A success message from the placeholder step is not evidence that a placeholder exists. The only evidence is the round-tripped story text.
trajectory.produces: A merge template with a placeholder audit taken from the re-exported IDML rather than from the tool response.

trajectory.action: Merge the line: cards for the twelve looks with each look's own prepared photograph bound per row, and produce the per-look card files the showroom needs.
trajectory.judgement: Binding is not naming. The image column follows the shoot's numbering in places and the line follows the look numbering, so identity has to be reconciled before the merge rather than assumed after it.
trajectory.produces: A press file with one card per look and a per-look card set.

trajectory.action: Render sign-off proofs at real resolution from the merged document rather than out of the merge call, and read each card against the line.
trajectory.judgement: Resolution asked for inside the merge is silently ignored, so a proof taken there is a screen-scale file wearing a print label. Reading each card against the line is the only way identity is confirmed.
trajectory.produces: Proofs at genuine resolution, with a per-card identity check written down.

trajectory.action: Author the lookbook HTML: a page per look, the range grid, the two essay pages set to an editorial measure, the linesheet price grid as a real table with one row per look, every photograph inlined as image data, the wordmark as inline SVG in an explicitly sized top-left anchored wrapper, family and weight declared on every text element.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, and an auto-sized right-anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas. The design work is the measure of the essay pages and how much held space a 600 to 2,400 dollar collection takes.
trajectory.produces: An export-ready lookbook HTML, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Author the campaign document: two poster roots as two genuinely different directions plus the square, four by five and tall social roots, each root declaring its own canvas, carrying the same kit and the same wordmark treatment.
trajectory.judgement: Two directions means two arguments, not one layout recoloured. A global canvas override is what collapses a mixed-size set, so sizes are declared per root and nothing is passed as a parameter.
trajectory.produces: An export-ready campaign HTML carrying the poster pair and the social canvases.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check before each export, export both documents by uploaded URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve each document's rendition and look at its first root, and parse the returned per-root markup for every other root.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition preview only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at page one is not looking at a fourteen-root lookbook.
trajectory.produces: Two native editable Express documents, two inspected first roots, and a per-root markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Create the press selects board, add the graded looks, the cutouts and the licensed ground within the per-call placement cap, re-sending only the entries the response names as failed, then write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: A 201 is partial success, and the vector wordmark is not boardable so it belongs in the note instead. The note has to be specific enough that the atelier can run next season without repeating the archaeology.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the two exterior frames can be brought to the collection's grey scale at all. They were shot against a white sky at the end of the day, and the highlights are already at the ceiling, so a highlight correction accepts its parameters, reports success and returns a frame in which nothing has moved. There is no error, no warning and no readout that says the data was not there to move, and the returned frame looks entirely plausible on its own because it looks exactly like the frame that went in. The mismatch only exists relative to the other ten looks, so it becomes visible when the twelve are laid out as a range and not before.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it, because the correction is applied before anyone can know whether it took, and the tool reports success either way. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the light was lost and two looks were taken outside, which describes a shooting circumstance, not a clipped file, and the acceptance line about the twelve reading as one collection is the atelier's standing requirement. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different decision about the whole set: move the collection's target to a scale those two frames can actually reach, treat them as a declared separate register, or name them as looks that cannot be brought in.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-decide the collection target against what the exterior frames can actually reach, re-grade the ten studio looks toward that revised target rather than the original one, re-assemble the range grid, and where the two still will not join, say so in writing and propose which look carries the cover instead.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A lookbook whose range grid has two blown pages sitting in the middle of it, going to press and to a buyer list on a collection whose whole argument is restraint and control.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether each showroom card actually carries the look it names. When the merge is taken as per-record raster files, the outputs come back in an order the response labels contradict, so the file labelled as the first record is not the first record, while every response reports success and every card looks correct on its own because each is a well-formed card. Nothing in the tool responses exposes it, the labels are confidently wrong, and the CSV's own image column follows the shoot's numbering rather than the look numbering on part of the line, so a wrong pairing looks exactly as plausible as a right one. It surfaces only by reading each rendered card against the line, look number, garment and price together.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, and doing it right first time is actively steered against: the client asked for one card per look as separate files, and the route whose own description promises one output file per row is the raster route, which is the one whose order lies. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for a card per look with that look's photograph on it, and the acceptance line about a card bound to the wrong look failing is the atelier's requirement, not a warning about output ordering. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different delivery route entirely, with identity guaranteed by construction rather than inferred from a returned list.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Abandon the per-record raster route, re-deliver through a route whose order is guaranteed, reconcile the image column against the look numbers before re-binding, re-merge, and re-read every card against the line rather than against the response, then re-render the proofs.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Twelve showroom cards handed to buyers with the wrong garment, the wrong fabric and the wrong wholesale price on them, on the single document the season's orders are written from.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the two constructs the editorial look is built on. The essay pages are set to a magazine measure, and the two-tone panels that carry the campaign directions are built as an overlay reading through the photograph beneath. Authored the natural way, the measure is a multi-column text flow and the overlay is a blend mode, and the importer drops the column structure so the text reflows as one column running past the page edge, and drops the blend so the panel renders as a plain opaque shape covering the photograph entirely. Both return success with no warning of any kind, the returned per-root markup is the only channel that reports either, and each document's rendition returns its first root only, so the essay pages and the second poster direction can be checked no other way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step, and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for essay pages and a poster pair, and the acceptance lines are about how the pages read. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is to build both differently, the measure as positioned text frames of a chosen width and the two-tone as an upstream raster treatment produced in the image pipeline, then to re-compose the pages around what actually survives.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-author the essay pages as explicitly measured text frames, produce the two-tone treatment in the imaging pipeline so it is part of the pixels rather than a page effect, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and audit every root from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A lookbook whose essay pages run off the trim edge and a poster direction that is a flat block of colour where the photograph should be, both delivered as editable files with every export reporting success and nobody having looked past page one.

deliverables.name: Nordheim FW26 house photography
deliverables.spec: The twelve looks brought to one grey editorial target, one black point, one grey scale, one figure height, across two shooting days and two lighting situations, with the printed texture applied as masked region-confined work so wool, shearling and gabardine still read as different materials at reproduction size, plus one licensed camera-scale ground carried through the same treatment. Per-frame parameter log including mask polarity and one line on why each frame differs from its neighbours.

deliverables.name: FW26 look cutouts
deliverables.spec: A cutout per look with genuine alpha that holds its edge on the pale garments as well as the dark ones, no bitten shoulder and no white rim when a look sits on a dark page, plus on-ground plates where a page needs one, every output at or below its source pixel dimensions with the returned tradeoff record for each. One set with one cutout logic, not one picture at several sizes.

deliverables.name: Recovered Nordheim wordmark
deliverables.spec: The compound letterpress lockup recovered as placeable scalable vector geometry with a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full-canvas rectangle riding along, all three elements present, the wordmark, the hairline rule and the small caps, delivered as a single-colour mark and a colour-accurate variant, complete at cover size, at poster size and small on a line card.

deliverables.name: Showroom line card run

decision_gates: Which deliverables are raster work, which are a genuine record-per-page run, and which need an authored fixed-canvas document, given that only one surface composes free-form layout and only one does volume personalisation.
What the collection's grey target actually is, decided against what every frame can reach rather than against the strongest frame alone.
How far to carry the two exterior frames before they stop being worth carrying, versus declaring them a separate register or naming them.
Knockout route per look: the one-call route for the dark garments versus a material-named ground selection inverted and filled for the undyed wool whose shoulder shares luminance with the seamless.
Mask polarity and texture radius: what carries the dot and what stays clean, judged at the size the piece actually reproduces rather than at preview scale.
Selection wording on the letterpress card: naming the substrate takes the card, naming the whole lockup silently returns part of it, and background removal is the wrong instrument on lettering.
What the converted line card actually exposes as mappable structure, and what a mapping can honestly promise once that is known.
How look identity is guaranteed across the card run when the image column follows one numbering and the line follows another, and which delivery route makes that guarantee by construction.

The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged as documentary editorial rather than fashion-glossy, plus the real numeric weight per family and whether the display cut is reached by slug.
Whether a licensed ground joins the world the twelve looks live in or reads as bought.
How dense the lookbook pages are. At this band held space is the argument, and a full, benefit-led page is a correct-looking wrong answer.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of fashion. IDENTITY: these are this atelier's twelve actual FW26 garments in their actual fabrics, photographed on the actual fit, and the wordmark must be RECOVERED off a letterpress card rather than reinvented, because a regenerated garment is not the garment a buyer will receive and a regenerated wordmark is a different label. SPEC: the showroom needs one card per look off the atelier's own printed artwork with that look's own photograph, that look's own fabric wording and that look's own wholesale and retail prices, in line order, and a generated image cannot satisfy or be checked against any of that. EDITABILITY: the lookbook, linesheet, posters and social are defined by being editable, because the line moves during the selling season and a small atelier cannot re-commission. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this highlight correction move anything, is this card actually the look it names, did the essay measure survive the import.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, monochromatic_tint, halftone with a mask and blackAndWhite, add_grain, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, select_subject, invert_selection, fill_area, remove_background, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs, and vectorize are verified headless across 27 live calls, including the masked-polarity move where an inverted mask dotted the field at a chosen radius while the lettering stayed crisp. The checkpoints rest on documented findings: selection is unreliably partial on compound marks (a badge prompt silently dropped the inner rule and the central element), remove_background returns a solid opaque plate on lettering (1,743 opaque pixels out of roughly 18,000 of ink), halftone has radius only and no frequency control so reproduction size is the only judge, and remove_background silently downscales oversized inputs. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout and document_render_layout are verified fully headless and synchronous end to end, a printed card was reverse-engineered into a live merge template, per-row image binding through an at-prefixed column plus additionalImageFiles was visually confirmed to bind the right image to the right row, PDF output is one record per page with page count equal to row count, and document_render_layout returns true 300 dpi while outputSpecs.resolution inside the merge is silently ignored. The card checkpoint rests on the verified finding that multi-record raster outputs came back REVERSED while their labels claimed row order, with PDF, createSeparateFiles and a recordRange loop all verified correct. Frame granularity from a PDF is documented as not under the author's control, with a continuous flow collapsing to a single text frame. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export, real tables with per-cell shapes and text, inline SVG as native editable vector, fixed-measure versus auto-sizing text frames, and a genuine editable dcx findable by asset_search are all verified, while column-count is dropped and reflows as one column and mix-blend-mode is dropped to a plain opaque shape, both at HTTP success, and the rendition preview is documented as first root only. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the 70 KB threshold immediately. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit verified end to end including the all-or-nothing kit call and non-standard numeric weights. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, license returned a real 7360x4912 JPEG, boards persist with a hard cap of 12 placements per call and 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no bleed or press-preset claim, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text-to-image, no fill_text, no animate_design, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no batch above 20.
